claim: Propranolol can alter later conditioned fear expression when paired with memory reactivation
rationale: Multiple human studies and 2026 systematic review support a laboratory effect but modality/paradigm inconsistency remains

claim: Propranolol plus trauma-memory reactivation reduces PTSD symptoms more than placebo
rationale: Brunet positive signal conflicts with Roullet null and 2022 vs 2025 meta-analytic conclusions; clinical effect remains uncertain

claim: Retrieval-extinction reliably prevents return of conditioned fear in humans
rationale: Influential positive original result is weakened by reanalysis and negative preregistered replication

claim: Prediction error is a relevant moderator of post-retrieval fear-memory updating
rationale: Several studies support PE relevance but precise boundary rules have failed replication and operationalizations vary

claim: A single prediction error universally triggers fear-memory destabilization
rationale: Direct failed replication and null PE-type studies argue against a universal one-PE rule

claim: Memory strength moderates retrieval-extinction/reconsolidation effects in humans
rationale: New 2025 direct study is relevant but independent replication and full effect extraction are lacking

claim: PTSD symptom improvement after reactivation demonstrates reconsolidation as the mechanism
rationale: Clinical symptom change does not isolate reconsolidation from exposure extinction expectancy contact or nonspecific pharmacology
